content.text: Let me check the README and look for documentation/behavior mismatches.

# במבט

Hebrew news in perspective: publisher categories, dry headlines, links to original
articles, and a broad reading order that rotates categories and sources. Difficult
news remains visible. No sentiment scoring, viral ranking, infinite scrolling,
sensational imagery, or tracking.

## Name

The chosen name is **במבט** — a short, memorable Hebrew name for "news in
perspective". Hebrew taglines such as **חדשות בפרופורציה** and
**אותן עובדות, פחות דרמה** carry the editorial promise. No English subtitle is
shown in the header or any visitor-facing branding. This is a product name only;
the repository, Worker and deployment identities are unchanged.

## Development

Node 24+:

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run dev
npm run check
npm test
npm run build
npm run test:worker   # Miniflare runtime check with fictional fixtures (builds first)
npm run test:browser  # headless Chromium render check (builds first, needs Chromium on PATH)
npm run test:interaction  # keyboard/interaction QA in headless Chromium (builds first)
```

The three `dist`-based checks rebuild the bundle first and refuse to run against a
missing or stale `dist/worker.js`, so a runtime check always exercises the current
source rather than an old build. `build` bundles the Worker with Wrangler's dry run;
it does not publish. Live
headlines are never replaced with sample articles. The first request starts a
bounded background refresh; reload after it finishes. Wrangler local development
needs outbound access to the publisher hosts for live aggregation. Additional
workerd checks: `npm run test:worker` (fixtures), `npm run test:extract`
(full-text extraction), `npm run test:retirement` (stale-cache retirement),
`npm run test:pipeline` (mock-model end-to-end), `npm run test:batch`
(validator-window batch splitting) and `npm run test:interaction` (keyboard Tab
traversal, source/category filters, chronological toggle, load-more pagination
and the rendered error/retry state).

## Cloudflare deployment

Use the existing **Cloudflare Workers Builds** connection to `main`:

- Install: `npm ci --ignore-scripts` (or Cloudflare's lockfile-based default install).
- Build command: `npm run check && npm test`.
- Deploy command: `npm run deploy` (`wrangler deploy`, not Pages deploy).
- Root directory: repository root. Node: 24.
- Worker name: `positivity-bias` in `wrangler.jsonc`; match the existing connected
  Worker if its name is different. Preserve its current routes and custom domain.

The SQLite Durable Object binding and migration are declared in Wrangler and are
created by deployment. No manual D1/KV database IDs are needed. The Worker refreshes
at minute 7 each hour (Cloudflare cron is UTC); public dates use Asia/Jerusalem.
The same Durable Object serializes refreshes and persists an hourly cooldown,
including after failures, so public reads cannot cause unbounded model usage.

This environment did not have Cloudflare account access, so the existing dashboard
commands and deployed URL could not be inspected. `npm run deploy` requires
Cloudflare authentication outside the connected Builds runner.

## Headline rewrites

Rewrites use **Cloudflare Workers AI**, with the native `AI` binding declared in
`wrangler.jsonc`. No inference API key is needed. The Actions OCGO key is only
for Shurik. The inexpensive default is `@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fp8-fast`.
The cheap allowlist also permits `@cf/qwen/qwen3-30b-a3b-fp8` (documented Hebrew
support, lower output price) and Llama 3.2 1B/3B. Expensive or paid-only models
are blocked. Qwen3's thinking phase is disabled and its chat-style response
envelope is handled; switching the default still requires measured Hebrew-quality
checks against the live account.

Each refresh fetches the **full accessible article text** for the candidates it can
afford, strips navigation, advertising and unrelated recommendations, and passes the
publisher, original headline, publication time and body (marked complete, truncated
or missing) to the model. The editorial prompt requires the primary point and its
material context — actor/speaker, action, geographic scope and result — and never
reverses an outcome. Missing context keeps the original headline.

A candidate is then checked with `@cf/cloudflare/clef-flash`, which answers two
separate questions: is every claim supported by the source, and are the primary point
and material context preserved without misleading omission, broadening, narrowing or
changed emphasis? A candidate is accepted only when both are true; anything
unsupported, incomplete or uncertain falls back to the preserved original.

Requests are sized adaptively from the actual full-text input, the context window,
reserved output space and the remaining daily budget. The same context goes to both
the rewrite model and the validator, so each request is limited to the **smaller** of
their context windows (`clef-flash` is 32,768 tokens) and output space is reserved per
article. The project reserves a
conservative slice of the shared **10,000-neuron/day** free allocation
(`DAILY_NEURON_BUDGET`, default 6000), persists the reservation before any model
call, reconciles it with provider-reported usage, and defers work instead of
overspending. No billing upgrade, retries or automatic budget increase.

Accepted rewrites are cached with a policy fingerprint covering the model, the
full-context extraction policy, the editorial prompt and the validator version, and
source-grounded rejections are cached by the same fingerprint plus a source-content
fingerprint. At read/serve time, and through a persisted idempotent migration, any
decision whose fingerprint does not match the active policy (or whose source content
changed) is retired: the generated headline is cleared, the original returns to
display, and the article is reprocessed progressively under the same daily budget.
Full article text is inference context only — it is never shown in the UI, returned
by the public API, or written to Git. The original remains visible, and rejected
numbers/uncertainty changes, newly added sensational framing, rhetorical questions,
outcome reversals and insufficient context all fall back to an explicitly labeled
original title. Automated guards cannot fully prove factual fidelity; editorial
review is still useful.

**No model classification is currently needed.** If a concrete classification
need arises, use `@cf/cloudflare/clef-flash` as requested. Categories come from RSS category fields,
publisher feed names, JSON-LD `articleSection`, or article metadata. Unknown stays
unknown. Root [`websites.json`](websites.json) controls the four initial publishers.
Each feed has a source-provided fallback label and explicit allowed hosts. N12
uses Mako's official syndication endpoint; shared Mako/N12 article IDs deduplicate.
Full accessible article text is used transiently for rewrite context and is never
returned by the public API or written to Git.
The archive retains up to 480 articles from the last 72 hours.

## Shurik on main

The one-time `Start main loop` push workflow starts `main` using
`igor-makarov/shurik@v1`, `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, high reasoning,
`PROMPT.md`, a 600-second work budget and `wait-seconds=0` so iterations continue
immediately.
It skips startup if `shurik-control/main` already exists. Only the iteration job
receives the model key. Supported repository secret names are `OPENCODE_API_KEY`,
`OCGO_API_KEY`, and `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` (the first set wins).

Shurik recovery runs every 15 minutes and restarts work after the saved due time;
the interval is approximate, not an exact hourly appointment. A separate hourly
Codex checkup reads source/control evidence and steers `PROMPT.md`; Shurik owns
implementation work. See
[`STATUS.md`](STATUS.md) for current evidence and next priorities.

Stop/resume via **Actions → Shurik → Run workflow** on `main`, `loop_id=main`.
Resume requires explicit reasoning (choose `high`). Blank work/wait inputs on resume
retain saved settings. `wait-seconds=0` resumes immediate continuation. Do not start
another loop on main. Control/session history is public in this public repository;
keep credentials only in secrets.

## Interface and API

- `/api/news`: `q`, `source`, exact `category`, `order=broad|latest`, `limit` (1–120),
  `offset`; includes category options, source states, freshness and original titles.
- `/api/status`: source/freshness/rewrite status. No key values or provider responses.
- No public refresh/admin endpoint. Cron invokes the internal Durable Object.
- A failed source does not replace the last successful articles; old articles expire
  after 72 hours. Stale or partial coverage is visible in the interface.

The UI follows the [Canton of Zürich design system](https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten.html),
adapted for Hebrew RTL: square controls, bold/regular type hierarchy, rules and a
clear grid. Black/white and gray carry content; #0070B4 blue/#EDF5FA soft blue mark
interaction. #1A7F1F green indicates a successful source update, not positive news.
The self-hosted Heebo font uses the bundled SIL Open Font License. No canton branding
or licensed Helvetica font assets are used.

## Verified (2026-10-13, iteration 2-9)

19. **Clef factual-verification call was fundamentally wrong and is now fixed.**
    `@cf/cloudflare/clef-flash` is a *decision* model, not a chat/completion model: its
    documented API takes `{ model, state, questions }` (typed `noul`/`choice`/`score`
    questions) and returns probabilities under `answers`. The previous verifier sent a
    chat envelope (`messages`, `response_format`, `temperature`, `max_tokens`) and parsed
    `choices`/`response`, which the real endpoint cannot accept, so in production every
    rewrite would have fallen back to its original and the refresh would report
    `provider_unavailable`. `verifyBatch` now builds the documented schema (two `noul`
    questions per candidate, keyed by candidate index for per-article independence),
    parses `answers[*].noul`, and accepts only when both probabilities are a confident
    yes. Requests are chunked to the documented 64-question limit; a non-clef validator
    is refused (`validator_misconfigured`). New unit regressions assert the exact request
    shape (no `messages`/`response_format`/`max_tokens`), that a chat-shaped response is
    never accepted as a verdict, and that uncertain/missing answers keep the original.
20. **Clef window, pricing and budget corrected to the documented values.** The
    validator window is 24,576 tokens (not 32,768) and clef charges input tokens only
    ($0.038/M → 0.0034545 neurons/token, no output charge). `requestContextTokens`,
    `MODEL_NEURON_RATES`/`MODEL_CONTEXT_TOKENS` and `estimateBatchNeurons` now reflect
    that, and the shared per-item reservation includes the two clef questions, so a
    rewrite+verify batch is sized for the real validator window without truncating
    article context. `VALIDATOR_VERSION` is bumped to `clef-guard-v2`, retiring any
    rewrite verified under the broken validator. `npm run test:batch` now reports the
    24,576-token window; all other checks are unchanged.

## Verified (2026-10-13, iteration 2-9)

19. **Clef factual-verification call was fundamentally wrong and is now fixed.**
    `@cf/cloudflare/clef-flash` is a *decision* model, not a chat/completion model: its
    documented API takes `{ model, state, questions }` (typed `noul`/`choice`/`score`
    questions) and returns probabilities under `answers`. The previous verifier sent a
    chat envelope (`messages`, `response_format`, `temperature`, `max_tokens`) and parsed
    `choices`/`response`, which the real endpoint cannot accept, so in production every
    rewrite would have fallen back to its original and the refresh would report
    `provider_unavailable`. `verifyBatch` now builds the documented schema (two `noul`
    questions per candidate, keyed by candidate index for per-article independence),
    parses `answers[*].noul`, and accepts only when both probabilities are a confident
    yes. Requests are chunked to the documented 64-question limit; a non-clef validator
    is refused (`validator_misconfigured`). New unit regressions assert the exact request
    shape (no `messages`/`response_format`/`max_tokens`), that a chat-shaped response is
    never accepted as a verdict, and that uncertain/missing answers keep the original.
20. **Clef window, pricing and budget corrected to the documented values.** The
    validator window is 24,576 tokens (not 32,768) and clef charges input tokens only
    ($0.038/M → 0.0034545 neurons/token, no output charge). `requestContextTokens`,
    `MODEL_NEURON_RATES`/`MODEL_CONTEXT_TOKENS` and `estimateBatchNeurons` now reflect
    that, and the shared per-item reservation includes the two clef questions, so a
    rewrite+verify batch is sized for the real validator window without truncating
    article context. `VALIDATOR_VERSION` is bumped to `clef-guard-v2`, retiring any
    rewrite verified under the broken validator. `npm run test:batch` now reports the
    24,576-token window; all other checks are unchanged.

Iteration 2-9 complete. Here's what I did and verified.

## Defect found and fixed (highest priority)

While auditing the AI path against the **official Cloudflare docs** (network was available), I found that `@cf/cloudflare/clef-flash` is a **decision model**, not a chat/completion model. Its documented API is `{ model, state, questions }` with typed `noul`/`choice`/`score` questions and returns probabilities under `answers`. The verifier was sending the chat envelope (`messages`, `response_format`, `temperature`, `max_tokens`) and parsing `choices`/`response` — a contract the real endpoint cannot accept. In production that would have made **every** rewrite fall back to its original and the refresh report `provider_unavailable`.

Fix:
- `verifyBatch` now builds the documented schema: one `state` array of candidates plus **two `noul` yes/no questions per candidate** (`supported`, `preserved`), keyed by candidate index for per-article independence. A candidate is accepted only when both probabilities are a confident yes; missing/uncertain answers keep the original.
- Chunking to the documented **64-question** and **24,576-token** limits; a non-clef validator is refused (`validator_misconfigured`).
- Corrected `MODEL_CONTEXT_TOKENS` (24,576, not 32,768), `MODEL_NEURON_RATES` (clef charges input only: $0.038/M → 0.0034545 neurons/token, 0 output), the shared per-item reservation (rewrite result + two questions), and bumped `VALIDATOR_VERSION` to `clef-guard-v2` so rewrites verified under the broken validator are retired.

## Verification
- `npm run check`, **54 unit tests**, `npm run build`.
- `test:worker`, `test:extract`, `test:retirement`, `test:pipeline`, `test:batch` (now reports the 24,576-token window), `test:browser`, `test:interaction` — all pass.
- New regressions assert the exact clef request shape (no `messages`/`response_format`/`max_tokens`), the documented question-limit constraints, that a chat-shaped response is never accepted as a verdict, and that uncertain/missing answers keep the original.
- Generated request validated against Cloudflare's published `schema-input.json`; a fail-before proof shows the old chat envelope misses the required `model`/`state`/`questions` fields.
- Live re-check: real ynet/mako article pages extracted `complete` bodies; a real refresh ingested **127 articles** across ynet/kan/n12/mako (all `ok`) and the new clef path accepted rewrites end-to-end under workerd.

Docs (`README.md`, `STATUS.md`) updated. One commit on `main`; working tree clean.

**Still needs live account access:** the semantic *quality* of clef's probabilities and the Qwen3 default switch (unmeasured Hebrew fidelity/neuron use) — the request/response contract now matches the published schema.

# Current state

- Hebrew RTL news Worker on `main`: configurable source registry; RSS/Atom and Kan
  news-sitemap adapters; category/source rotation; hourly ingestion; SQLite Durable
  Object storage; guarded Workers AI rewrites with originals preserved.
- Chosen name: **במבט**. English subtitle removed from the visible header/logo.
- Sessions/control are on `shurik-control/main`; iterations continue immediately
  (`wait-seconds: 0`), with a separate hourly Codex checkup.

## Verified (2026-10-13, iteration 2-9)

19. **Clef factual-verification call was fundamentally wrong and is now fixed.**
    `@cf/cloudflare/clef-flash` is a *decision* model, not a chat/completion model: its
    documented API takes `{ model, state, questions }` (typed `noul`/`choice`/`score`
    questions) and returns probabilities under `answers`. The previous verifier sent a
    chat envelope (`messages`, `response_format`, `temperature`, `max_tokens`) and parsed
    `choices`/`response`, which the real endpoint cannot accept, so in production every
    rewrite would have fallen back to its original and the refresh would report
    `provider_unavailable`. `verifyBatch` now builds the documented schema (two `noul`
    questions per candidate, keyed by candidate index for per-article independence),
    parses `answers[*].noul`, and accepts only when both probabilities are a confident
    yes. Requests are chunked to the documented 64-question limit; a non-clef validator
    is refused (`validator_misconfigured`). New unit regressions assert the exact request
    shape (no `messages`/`response_format`/`max_tokens`), that a chat-shaped response is
    never accepted as a verdict, and that uncertain/missing answers keep the original.
20. **Clef window, pricing and budget corrected to the documented values.** The
    validator window is 24,576 tokens (not 32,768) and clef charges input tokens only
    ($0.038/M → 0.0034545 neurons/token, no output charge). `requestContextTokens`,
    `MODEL_NEURON_RATES`/`MODEL_CONTEXT_TOKENS` and `estimateBatchNeurons` now reflect
    that, and the shared per-item reservation includes the two clef questions, so a
    rewrite+verify batch is sized for the real validator window without truncating
    article context. `VALIDATOR_VERSION` is bumped to `clef-guard-v2`, retiring any
    rewrite verified under the broken validator. `npm run test:batch` now reports the
    24,576-token window; all other checks are unchanged.

## Verified (2026-10-13, iteration 2-8)

16. **Budget-aware batch sizing.** `planBatches` sized requests by the context window
    only; the remaining daily neuron budget was a yes/no gate per pre-planned batch, so
    a batch larger than what was left deferred **every** article in it even though some
    could fit. New `estimateBatchNeurons`/`fitBatchToBudget` (`src/budget.js`) reduce a
    context-sized batch to the largest prefix whose estimated rewrite+verify cost fits
    the remaining budget, without truncating article context; `src/worker.js` uses them
    per request. This directly satisfies "size each request from the actual full-text
    input, model context window, reserved output space, and remaining daily neuron
    budget". Unit regressions cover the fit/truncate/overspend cases; `npm run test:batch`
    now runs a fresh Durable Object with a 60-neuron budget and proves one article is
    rewritten (1 rewrite + 1 verify call) instead of deferring all nine, with usage ≤ 60.
    The new integration assertion was shown to fail against the pre-fix per-batch gate
    (0 rewrite calls) and pass after the fix. Existing budget=0 deferral, full-budget
    throughput, retirement and reprocessing behaviour is unchanged.
17. **Lost-headline retirement hardening.** `retireStaleRewrites` only treated a stored
    headline as untrusted when it was a string that differed from the original, so a
    legacy/partial snapshot whose generated `headline` was missing (and had no
    status/fingerprint) was served with `headline: undefined` instead of the preserved
    original, violating the display invariant (and `mergeArticles` could propagate the
    missing headline). Any article whose stored headline is missing or differs from the
    preserved original is now retired to the original. New unit and
    `npm run test:retirement` regressions cover a headless article and were shown to
    fail against the pre-fix logic and pass after it.
18. **Article-level serve-time enforcement.** `applyPolicyRetirement` returned early
    whenever the snapshot-level `policyFingerprint` already matched, so an inconsistent
    snapshot (flag advanced while an article still held a stale/headless cached headline)
    would keep serving it until the next refresh. The check now runs against the actual
    article state on every read and writes only when something changed; a current-policy
    accepted rewrite is still kept. `npm run test:retirement` seeds the active fingerprint
    together with a stale and a headless headline and proves both are retired on read while
    the trusted rewrite is served; the assertion was shown to fail against the pre-fix
    early return and pass after it.

## Verified (2026-10-13, iteration 2-7)

14. **Missing-fingerprint retirement defect fixed.** `retireStaleRewrites` treated an
    article as having a decision only when `rewriteStatus` was `rewritten`/`rejected`
    or a fingerprint existed. A legacy/partial snapshot that lost both but still held
    a wrong generated `headline` was therefore served as a generated headline,
    violating "missing fingerprints must never expose an untrusted cached rewrite."
    Now any stored headline that differs from the preserved original is treated as an
    untrusted rewrite and retired to the original. New unit regression fails on the
    pre-fix logic and passes after it; `npm run test:retirement` seeds such an orphan
    article (no status, no fingerprint) into the real Worker and confirms it is never
    served and the migration persists.
15. **Qwen3 response-shape handling hardened.** `parseModelText` now resolves chat
    `choices` under top-level, `result` and `response` wrappers; `modelUsageNeurons`
    also reads nested `result.usage`; a thinking-only `reasoning_content` with empty
    `content` is not mistaken for the JSON result. New unit and batch regressions
    cover the nested Qwen3 envelope. Default model remains Llama pending the live
    Hebrew/neuron measurement described under Blocked.

## Verified (2026-10-13, iteration 2-6)

11. **Runtime checks now exercise current source.** `test:worker`, `test:browser` and
    `test:interaction` rebuild the bundle first, and new `scripts/bundle-guard.js`
    refuses a missing or stale `dist/worker.js` (compared by mtime against `src/`,

    old build, and a direct `node scripts/smoke.js` exits with a clear message instead
    of an ENOENT stack. The esbuild-based checks already read `src/` directly.
12. **Retire→reprocess regression.** `npm run test:pipeline` now seeds a stale wrong
    cached headline for a fixture article, runs the real refresh with the mock model,
    and asserts the wrong headline is never served while the article is reprocessed

6. **Shared batch sizing fix.** `planBatches` previously sized requests by the

   now sized for the **smaller** of the rewrite and validator windows

7. **Interactive-QA API coverage.** `scripts/smoke.js` now also checks category

## Verified (2026-10-13, iteration 2-3)

0. **Branding correction.** Removed the `POSITIVITY BIAS` span from
   `public/index.html` and the now-unused `.brand-caption` rules and reserved

1. **Full-text grounding.** `src/extract.js` extracts the article body with one

2. **Editorial + verification prompts.** The rewrite prompt now requires the primary

    steps:

    Fix clef-flash verification: use its documented decision schema
    
    @cf/cloudflare/clef-flash is a decision model (state + typed questions ->
    answers), not a chat model. The verifier sent messages/response_format/
    max_tokens and parsed choices/response, which the real endpoint cannot
    accept, so in production every rewrite would fall back to its original.
    verifyBatch now sends two noul questions per candidate (keyed by index)
    and accepts only when both probabilities are confidently yes; requests
    are chunked to the documented 64-question/24,576-token limits and a
    non-clef validator is refused. Clef window (24,576), input-only pricing
    and the shared per-item reservation are corrected, and VALIDATOR_VERSION
    is bumped to retire rewrites verified under the broken validator.

# Current state

- Hebrew RTL news Worker on `main`: configurable source registry; RSS/Atom and Kan
  news-sitemap adapters; category/source rotation; hourly ingestion; SQLite Durable
  Object storage; guarded Workers AI rewrites with originals preserved.
- Chosen name: **במבט**. English subtitle removed from the visible header/logo.
- Sessions/control are on `shurik-control/main`; iterations continue immediately
  (`wait-seconds: 0`), with a separate hourly Codex checkup.

## Verified (2026-10-13, iteration 2-10)

21. **Clef acceptance boundary corrected (uncertain verdicts now keep the original).**
    The guard accepted a candidate when both `noul` probabilities were `>= 0.5`, so a
    maximally uncertain 0.5 verdict — and any weak lean-yes — was treated as a confident
    yes, contradicting the code's own comment and the requirement to keep the original
    when a check is uncertain. `CLEF_ACCEPT_PROBABILITY` is now `0.7` (documented
    confident-yes boundary; values at or above it accept, everything lower keeps the
    preserved original). `VALIDATOR_VERSION` is bumped to `clef-guard-v3` so any rewrite
    verified under the looser boundary is retired by the existing fingerprint path and
    reprocessed progressively. The clef request/response contract was re-checked against
    the live Cloudflare docs (`state` may be structured JSON; `questions` are typed
    `noul`/`choice`/`score`, 1–64, with `criteria` valid for `noul`; `answers[id].noul` is
    the probability the answer is yes) — the verifier already matches it. New unit
    regression fails against the old `0.5` boundary and passes after the fix.
    Live re-check (2-10): two live ynet article pages exposed JSON-LD `articleBody`
    (1,925 and 2,826 chars) with no bot-block interstitial, so full-text grounding
    still works on real accessible articles; ynet categories come from its RSS labels.
    `articleSection` was absent on those pages, matching the policy that missing
    publisher categories stay missing.

22. **Unparseable model output is no longer reported as a healthy rewrite.** When the
    rewrite model returned JSON that could not be parsed, the refresh kept the originals
    (correct) but still recorded the snapshot `rewriteStatus` as `ok`, so a silently
    failing pipeline looked healthy. The run now tracks `invalid_response` and reports
    that status when nothing was accepted; originals are preserved and no rejection is
    cached, so the articles are retried on the next refresh. `npm run test:pipeline`
    seeds a mock that returns unparseable output and asserts the honest status, zero
    verification calls and untouched originals; the assertion was shown to fail (`ok`)
    against the pre-fix status logic and pass after it.

## Verified (2026-10-13, iteration 2-9)

19. **Clef factual-verification call was fundamentally wrong and is now fixed.**
    `@cf/cloudflare/clef-flash` is a *decision* model, not a chat/completion model: its
    documented API takes `{ model, state, questions }` (typed `noul`/`choice`/`score`
    questions) and returns probabilities under `answers`. The previous verifier sent a
    chat envelope (`messages`, `response_format`, `temperature`, `max_tokens`) and parsed
    `choices`/`response`, which the real endpoint cannot accept, so in production every
    rewrite would have fallen back to its original and the refresh would report
    `provider_unavailable`. `verifyBatch` now builds the documented schema (two `noul`
    questions per candidate, keyed by candidate index for per-article independence),
    parses `answers[*].noul`, and accepts only when both probabilities are a confident
    yes. Requests are chunked to the documented 64-question limit; a non-clef validator
    is refused (`validator_misconfigured`). New unit regressions assert the exact request
    shape (no `messages`/`response_format`/`max_tokens`), that a chat-shaped response is
    never accepted as a verdict, and that uncertain/missing answers keep the original.
20. **Clef window, pricing and budget corrected to the documented values.** The
    validator window is 24,576 tokens (not 32,768) and clef charges input tokens only
    ($0.038/M → 0.0034545 neurons/token, no output charge). `requestContextTokens`,
    `MODEL_NEURON_RATES`/`MODEL_CONTEXT_TOKENS` and `estimateBatchNeurons` now reflect
    that, and the shared per-item reservation includes the two clef questions, so a
    rewrite+verify batch is sized for the real validator window without truncating
    article context. `VALIDATOR_VERSION` is bumped to `clef-guard-v2`, retiring any
    rewrite verified under the broken validator. `npm run test:batch` now reports the
    24,576-token window; all other checks are unchanged.

## Verified (2026-10-13, iteration 2-8)

16. **Budget-aware batch sizing.** `planBatches` sized requests by the context window
    only; the remaining daily neuron budget was a yes/no gate per pre-planned batch, so
    a batch larger than what was left deferred **every** article in it even though some
    could fit. New `estimateBatchNeurons`/`fitBatchToBudget` (`src/budget.js`) reduce a
    context-sized batch to the largest prefix whose estimated rewrite+verify cost fits
    the remaining budget, without truncating article context; `src/worker.js` uses them
    per request. This directly satisfies "size each request from the actual full-text
    input, model context window, reserved output space, and remaining daily neuron
    budget". Unit regressions cover the fit/truncate/overspend cases; `npm run test:batch`
    now runs a fresh Durable Object with a 60-neuron budget and proves one article is
    rewritten (1 rewrite + 1 verify call) instead of deferring all nine, with usage ≤ 60.
    The new integration assertion was shown to fail against the pre-fix per-batch gate
    (0 rewrite calls) and pass after the fix. Existing budget=0 deferral, full-budget
    throughput, retirement and reprocessing behaviour is unchanged.
17. **Lost-headline retirement hardening.** `retireStaleRewrites` only treated a stored
    headline as untrusted when it was a string that differed from the original, so a
    legacy/partial snapshot whose generated `headline` was missing (and had no
    status/fingerprint) was served with `headline: undefined` instead of the preserved
    original, violating the display invariant (and `mergeArticles` could propagate the
    missing headline). Any article whose stored headline is missing or differs from the
    preserved original is now retired to the original. New unit and
    `npm run test:retirement` regressions cover a headless article and were shown to
    fail against the pre-fix logic and pass after it.
18. **Article-level serve-time enforcement.** `applyPolicyRetirement` returned early
    whenever the snapshot-level `policyFingerprint` already matched, so an inconsistent
    snapshot (flag advanced while an article still held a stale/headless cached headline)
    would keep serving it until the next refresh. The check now runs against the actual
    article state on every read and writes only when something changed; a current-policy
    accepted rewrite is still kept. `npm run test:retirement` seeds the active fingerprint
    together with a stale and a headless headline and proves both are retired on read while
    the trusted rewrite is served; the assertion was shown to fail against the pre-fix
    early return and pass after it.

## Verified (2026-10-13, iteration 2-7)

14. **Missing-fingerprint retirement defect fixed.** `retireStaleRewrites` treated an
    article as having a decision only when `rewriteStatus` was `rewritten`/`rejected`
    or a fingerprint existed. A legacy/partial snapshot that lost both but still held
    a wrong generated `headline` was therefore served as a generated headline,
    violating "missing fingerprints must never expose an untrusted cached rewrite."
    Now any stored headline that differs from the preserved original is treated as an
    untrusted rewrite and retired to the original. New unit regression fails on the
    pre-fix logic and passes after it; `npm run test:retirement` seeds such an orphan
    article (no status, no fingerprint) into the real Worker and confirms it is never
    served and the migration persists.
15. **Qwen3 response-shape handling hardened.** `parseModelText` now resolves chat
    `choices` under top-level, `result` and `response` wrappers; `modelUsageNeurons`
    also reads nested `result.usage`; a thinking-only `reasoning_content` with empty
    `content` is not mistaken for the JSON result. New unit and batch regressions
    cover the nested Qwen3 envelope. Default model remains Llama pending the live

11. **Runtime checks now exercise current source.** `test:worker`, `test:browser` and

13. **Deploy-migration regression made faithful.** `npm run test:retirement` now seeds

# במבט

Hebrew news in perspective: publisher categories, dry headlines, links to original
articles, and a broad reading order that rotates categories and sources. Difficult
news remains visible. No sentiment scoring, viral ranking, infinite scrolling,
sensational imagery, or tracking.

## Name

The chosen name is **במבט** — a short, memorable Hebrew name for "news in
perspective". Hebrew taglines such as **חדשות בפרופורציה** and
**אותן עובדות, פחות דרמה** carry the editorial promise. No English subtitle is
shown in the header or any visitor-facing branding. This is a product name only;
the repository, Worker and deployment identities are unchanged.

## Development

Node 24+:

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run dev
npm run check
npm test
npm run build
npm run test:worker   # Miniflare runtime check with fictional fixtures (builds first)
npm run test:browser  # headless Chromium render check (builds first, needs Chromium on PATH)
npm run test:interaction  # keyboard/interaction QA in headless Chromium (builds first)
```

The three `dist`-based checks rebuild the bundle first and refuse to run against a
missing or stale `dist/worker.js`, so a runtime check always exercises the current
source rather than an old build. `build` bundles the Worker with Wrangler's dry run;
it does not publish. Live
headlines are never replaced with sample articles. The first request starts a
bounded background refresh; reload after it finishes. Wrangler local development
needs outbound access to the publisher hosts for live aggregation. Additional
workerd checks: `npm run test:worker` (fixtures), `npm run test:extract`
(full-text extraction), `npm run test:retirement` (stale-cache retirement),
`npm run test:pipeline` (mock-model end-to-end), `npm run test:batch`
(validator-window batch splitting) and `npm run test:interaction` (keyboard Tab
traversal, source/category filters, chronological toggle, load-more pagination
and the rendered error/retry state).

## Cloudflare deployment

Use the existing **Cloudflare Workers Builds** connection to `main`:

- Install: `npm ci --ignore-scripts` (or Cloudflare's lockfile-based default install).
- Build command: `npm run check && npm test`.
- Deploy command: `npm run deploy` (`wrangler deploy`, not Pages deploy).
- Root directory: repository root. Node: 24.
- Worker name: `positivity-bias` in `wrangler.jsonc`; match the existing connected
  Worker if its name is different. Preserve its current routes and custom domain.

The SQLite Durable Object binding and migration are declared in Wrangler and are
created by deployment. No manual D1/KV database IDs are needed. The Worker refreshes
at minute 7 each hour (Cloudflare cron is UTC); public dates use Asia/Jerusalem.
The same Durable Object serializes refreshes and persists an hourly cooldown,
including after failures, so public reads cannot cause unbounded model usage.

This environment did not have Cloudflare account access, so the existing dashboard
commands and deployed URL could not be inspected. `npm run deploy` requires
Cloudflare authentication outside the connected Builds runner.

import { readdir, readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import configuration from '../websites.json' with { type: 'json' };
import { validateWebsites } from '../src/news.js';

validateWebsites(configuration);
for (const directory of ['src', 'public', 'scripts', 'test']) {
  for (const file of await readdir(directory)) {
    if (!file.endsWith('.js')) continue;
    const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, ['--check', `${directory}/${file}`], { stdio: 'inherit' });
    if (result.status !== 0) process.exit(result.status || 1);
  }
}
const config = JSON.parse(await readFile('wrangler.jsonc', 'utf8'));
if (config.main !== 'src/worker.js' || !config.durable_objects.bindings.some((binding) => binding.name === 'NEWS')) throw new Error('Missing Worker configuration');
for (const file of ['public/index.html', 'public/style.css', 'public/app.js', 'public/fonts/heebo.ttf', 'public/fonts/OFL.txt', 'PROMPT.md']) await readFile(file);
console.log('Source syntax, source registry, Worker configuration, and assets checked.');
// Guards the dist-based runtime checks so they exercise the CURRENT source instead of
// a stale or missing Wrangler bundle. `npm run test:worker|browser|interaction` build
// first; a direct `node scripts/...` run refuses rather than silently validating old
// code. The esbuild-based checks (extract/retirement/pipeline/batch) read `src/`
// directly and need no guard.
import { existsSync, readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';

const SOURCE_ROOTS = ['src', 'websites.json', 'package.json'];

function newestSourceMtime() {
  let newest = 0;
  const visit = (path) => {
    const stat = statSync(path);
    if (stat.isDirectory()) { for (const entry of readdirSync(path)) visit(`${path}/${entry}`); }
    else newest = Math.max(newest, stat.mtimeMs);
  };
  for (const path of SOURCE_ROOTS) if (existsSync(path)) visit(path);
  return newest;
}

export function requireFreshBundle(command) {
  if (!existsSync('dist/worker.js')) {
    console.error(`dist/worker.js is missing; run \`npm run build\` before \`${command}\`.`);
    process.exit(2);
  }
  if (statSync('dist/worker.js').mtimeMs < newestSourceMtime()) {
    console.error(`dist/worker.js is older than the source; run \`npm run build\` before \`${command}\`.`);
    process.exit(2);
  }
}

An article with `rewriteStatus: 'rejected'`, current fingerprint, and matching `rewriteSource` is trusted → kept as rejected. The API maps rewriteStatus to 'original' and serves `headline` = originalHeadline (since rejected articles keep headline=original). Good.

BUT: what if a `rejected` article was cached, and later the policy fingerprint matches but the article's `headline` field somehow holds a generated headline (i.e., the article was first 'rewritten' and then 'rejected' without resetting headline)? That means the client would show a generated headline but label it as original and NOT show the "original headline" details. # במבט

Hebrew news in perspective: publisher categories, dry headlines, links to original
articles, and a broad reading order that rotates categories and sources. Difficult
news remains visible. No sentiment scoring, viral ranking, infinite scrolling,
sensational imagery, or tracking.

## Name

The chosen name is **במבט** — a short, memorable Hebrew name for "news in
perspective". Hebrew taglines such as **חדשות בפרופורציה** and
**אותן עובדות, פחות דרמה** carry the editorial promise. No English subtitle is
shown in the header or any visitor-facing branding. This is a product name only;
the repository, Worker and deployment identities are unchanged.

## Development

Node 24+:

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run dev
npm run check
npm test
npm run build
npm run test:worker   # Miniflare runtime check with fictional fixtures (builds first)
npm run test:browser  # headless Chromium render check (builds first, needs Chromium on PATH)
npm run test:interaction  # keyboard/interaction QA in headless Chromium (builds first)
```

The three `dist`-based checks rebuild the bundle first and refuse to run against a
missing or stale `dist/worker.js`, so a runtime check always exercises the current
source rather than an old build. `build` bundles the Worker with Wrangler's dry run;
it does not publish. Live
headlines are never replaced with sample articles. The first request starts a
bounded background refresh; reload after it finishes. Wrangler local development
needs outbound access to the publisher hosts for live aggregation. Additional
workerd checks: `npm run test:worker` (fixtures), `npm run test:extract`
(full-text extraction), `npm run test:retirement` (stale-cache retirement),
`npm run test:pipeline` (mock-model end-to-end), `npm run test:batch`
(validator-window batch splitting) and `npm run test:interaction` (keyboard Tab
traversal, source/category filters, chronological toggle, load-more pagination
and the rendered error/retry state).

## Cloudflare deployment

Use the existing **Cloudflare Workers Builds** connection to `main`:

- Install: `npm ci --ignore-scripts` (or Cloudflare's lockfile-based default install).
- Build command: `npm run check && npm test`.
- Deploy command: `npm run deploy` (`wrangler deploy`, not Pages deploy).
- Root directory: repository root. Node: 24.
- Worker name: `positivity-bias` in `wrangler.jsonc`; match the existing connected
  Worker if its name is different. Preserve its current routes and custom domain.

The SQLite Durable Object binding and migration are declared in Wrangler and are
created by deployment. No manual D1/KV database IDs are needed. The Worker refreshes
at minute 7 each hour (Cloudflare cron is UTC); public dates use Asia/Jerusalem.
The same Durable Object serializes refreshes and persists an hourly cooldown,
including after failures, so public reads cannot cause unbounded model usage.

## Verified (2026-10-13, iteration 2-13)

28. **A cached rejection could be served as a generated headline labelled "original".**
    `retireStaleRewrites` trusted any `rejected` article whose policy fingerprint and
    `rewriteSource` matched the active policy, without checking that its stored
    `headline` was actually the preserved original. A partial/corrupted/legacy snapshot
    could therefore leave `rejected` carrying a generated headline; the public API maps
    every non-`rewritten` status to `original`, so the visitor would see the rewrite as
    if the publisher had written it, with no original-headline disclosure. A cached
    rejection is now trusted only when it carries the preserved original headline
    (`showsOriginal`); anything else is retired to the original like any stale rewrite.
    The restore step also keeps an existing headline when a malformed snapshot has no
    original to restore, so nothing is blanked. New unit regression (`60` unit tests)
    and a `npm run test:retirement` seeded current-fingerprint rejection with a generated
    headline: both were shown to fail against the pre-fix trust condition (the generated
    headline was served) and pass after it, while a genuine cached rejection
    (`headline === originalHeadline`) is still trusted and never re-inferred.
29. **Live full-text extraction re-measured on real publisher articles (fresh run).**
    Real feeds ingested `ok`: ynet 115, kan 8, n12 74, mako 61. Sampled contexts:
    ynet `complete` 1,920/2,384/2,688 chars, N12 `complete` 4,487, mako `complete` 908;
    a sampled mako request was answered with a Radware `validate.perfdrive.com`
    challenge and correctly refused (`unapproved_redirect`, original kept — the pipeline
    does not follow bot challenges). The live kan feed contains the exact reported
    drone-test headline (`...השלימה בהצלחה ניסוי במל״ט שמצויד במקלע`, kan-news/defense/1108988),
    but kan article pages are client-rendered shells (42 chars → `missing`), so that
    article keeps its preserved original rather than being rewritten from chrome.
    Context completeness stays transient and is never persisted or exposed.

## Verified (2026-10-13, iteration 2-12)

26. **A model omission was cached as a source-grounded rejection.** `rewritePending`
    cached a rejection for every non-accepted article whenever the batch status was
    `ok`/`partial`/`rejected`, even though its own comment promised to cache only
    "source-grounded rejections". When the model returned fewer items than requested
    (`partial`), the omitted articles were marked `rejected` with a matching
    `rewriteSource`, so `needsRewrite` skipped them forever and they were never retried.

**Concrete defect fixed (src/policy.js).**
`retireStaleRewrites` trusted any `rejected` article whose policy fingerprint and `rewriteSource` matched the active policy, without checking its stored `headline`. A partial/corrupted/legacy snapshot could leave `rejected` holding a *generated* headline; the public API maps every non-`rewritten` status to `original`, so the visitor would see the rewrite presented as the publisher's own headline with no original-headline disclosure. A cached rejection is now trusted only when it actually carries the preserved original headline (`showsOriginal`); otherwise it is retired to the original like any other stale rewrite. The restore step also refuses to blank an article when a malformed snapshot has no original to restore.

- `scripts/retirement-check.js`: seeds the same polluted rejection into the real Worker and asserts the served headline is the preserved original, with no inference available.
